correctness.rationale: For every rooted tree with at least four vertices, the root, leaf, and cover-edge hyperplanes are exactly its order-polytope facets. Root-deletion and leaf-deletion facets are isometric to product or smaller order polytopes; equality on a cover edge produces the Euclidean factor sqrt(2) relative to the contracted tree. Their hook-volume sum yields the exact boundary area. The path, fork, broom, and star profiles and their two gaps follow by exact rational counts. If one rooted poset has more relations than another on the same ground set, its order polytope is included in the other's. Proper full-dimensional inclusion strictly increases all conventional intrinsic volumes by Kubota's projection integral. Every rooted tree is bounded by the path and star, and every intermediate tree admits the fork lower extension and broom upper relaxation, with equality only at the corresponding rooted-tree type. An executable checker independently computed 59 Euclidean convex hull boundary areas and exhaustively classified 1,803 rooted profiles through dimension ten; those tests are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The goal is the natural extremal geometry of canonical rooted-tree order polytopes, an infinite family, not an arbitrarily selected finite slice. The theorem classifies first and second extremizers with strict equality cases for every Euclidean intrinsic volume at once. The deletion/contraction expression gives exact surface area for all rooted trees. The quantified gaps reveal opposite asymptotic scales: factorial decay at the small-volume end and a positive constant at the large end. The classification goes beyond restating Stanley's volume formula, and is useful for comparing metric properties of order bodies that differ in branching. It does not claim broader theorems for arbitrary posets.
